fields.h1: Build a PIP Form Template That Holds Every Goal to a Date
fields.hero_description: Build a PIP form template that saves only measurable goals, logs each check-in, and keeps every plan in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a PIP Needs After the Meeting Ends
fields.features_subheading: Describe the plan you run. Emergent builds the form, the check-in schedule, and the record HR reads when the end date arrives.
fields.feature_1:
Goals saved only with a number and a date

Write a vague goal such as better call quality and the form asks for the measure, the target, and the due date before saving it. Both people know on day one what meeting it means.
fields.feature_2:
The current result beside the expected one

Each concern takes two values: where the employee stands today and the standard the role expects. The gap reads as a number on the plan, not as an adjective in a paragraph.
fields.feature_3:
A log of the support the company promised

List the training, shadowing, or weekly one-on-ones the plan offers. The manager records each session as it happens. A week with no session shows as a blank row on the plan record.
fields.feature_4:
Check-in reminders that carry only a link

The manager gets an email before each scheduled check-in. It holds a link to the plan and nothing else, so no goal, score or comment sits in an inbox or a shared channel.
fields.feature_5:
Signed by the employee and the manager

Both people sign the plan on a phone or a laptop when it starts, and again when it closes. The employee also gets a comments box of their own, saved with the signed record.
fields.feature_6:
Your plan records, exportable as code

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and run the form next to the HR system you already use. Every plan, note, and outcome stays in tables you own.

fields.usecase_heading: Where a Plan Gets Used, Week by Week
fields.tab_content_1:
For a sales goal to save, it needs a number and a date

Dana Kilburn writes a 60-day plan for rep #207 at Garnock Office Supply. Her first goal reads book more demos, and the form will not save it. She rewrites it as 8 booked demos a month, then adds 50 logged calls a week as the second goal. Each one carries its own due date before the plan goes to the rep.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two coaching sessions a week, each one logged

Agent #3318 started a plan at Hattersley Software with a QA score of 71 and a target of 85. The plan promises 2 coaching sessions a week with team lead Joel Ravenscroft. He logs each session with its date and the calls they reviewed. By week 3 the score is 78, and all 6 sessions are on the record.
fields.tab_content_3:
An email 2 days ahead of each check-in

Every other Thursday, supervisor Nadia Truscott meets picker #1046 at Cobbridge Logistics. Two days before each meeting she gets an email that links to the plan and shows no details from it. At the week 4 check-in she opens the link and marks the error goal met: 3 picking errors in 2 weeks against a limit of 4.
fields.tab_content_4:
Of 7 open plans, the one past its end date

Gail Wainscott runs HR for the 4 stores of Vintry Pharmacy and sees all 7 open plans in one view, sorted by end date. Two of them end this week. One ended 3 days ago with no outcome recorded. It sits at the top in red until the store manager closes it.

fields.hero_prompt: Build a PIP form template for my managers where every goal needs a number and a due date.

faq_plan.q: What is a pip form template?
How do I create a pip form template?

plan.angle: The results for this query are downloadable Word, PDF and Excel PIP templates and HR guides that list the sections (the gap, the expected standard, goals, support, timeline, signatures). A file stops at the meeting. This page shows a working PIP form that keeps going after it: goals that will not save without a number and a date, the coaching the company promised logged as it happens, a reminder before each check-in that carries only a link, and an HR view of every open plan and its end date, all saved to a database the employer owns. No legal or HR-law advice; the copy gives instructions, not requirements.
tab_stories: At Garnock Office Supply, sales manager Dana Kilburn writes a 60-day plan for rep #207, and the form refuses a goal until it has a number and a due date: 8 booked demos a month and 50 logged calls a week.
At Hattersley Software, team lead Joel Ravenscroft logs the 2 coaching sessions a week the plan promised agent #3318, whose QA score has moved from 71% toward the 85% target.

At Cobbridge Logistics, supervisor Nadia Truscott gets an email 2 days before each biweekly check-in for picker #1046, with a link and no details, and marks the error goal met at 3 errors against a limit of 4.
At Vintry Pharmacy, HR lead Gail Wainscott sees 7 open plans across 4 stores; 2 end this week, and one passed its end date with no outcome recorded, so it sits at the top in red.
